title: Lachin–Khankendi road sit-in over mine monitoring
current_unit_observation: Reported active during January; search-result leads continue into February, with no confirmed end date.
location: Khankendi/Stepanakert–Lachin corridor near Shusha. TIME describes the area as within internationally recognized Azerbaijan borders but under de facto Artsakh administration and Russian peacekeeping control; Anadolu describes areas under temporary Russian military control.
organizer: Self-described Azerbaijani environmental activists; Anadolu also describes NGO representatives. Allegations of state orchestration are attributed in TIME and not treated as verified.
demands: Monitoring the Qizilbulag and Demirli mines and stopping alleged illegal exploitation/environmental harm. Whether the demand is directed at Azerbaijan’s government, Armenian de facto authorities, or Russian peacekeepers is unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: Neither opened article gives a participant count. The 50-person threshold is not established.

start_date.summary: Both opened Jan 2023 articles date the sit-in start to Dec 12, 2022.

continuity_into_january.summary: Opened articles describe it as ongoing on Jan 14 and Jan 18. Search-only titles separately identify reports for Jan 1 and the 51st day near January’s end.

location.summary: Sources describe an area under Russian peacekeeping control; TIME also distinguishes internationally recognized borders from de facto Artsakh governance.

organizer.summary: Anadolu identifies activists and NGOs; TIME uses self-described eco-protesters and attributes, but does not verify, the government-orchestration allegation.

demands.summary: Monitoring the Qizilbulag and Demirli mines; the target of the demand is not resolved.

attendance_threshold.summary: No captured evidence provides an attendance count or establishes at least 50 participants.

territorial_and_state_target.summary: Azerbaijan’s internationally recognized territorial claim, de facto Artsakh governance, Russian control and the demand’s recipient remain distinct questions; no automatic country transfer.

state_response.summary: Aliyev’s public supportive statements are reported, but no formal meeting, agreement to take up demands, or demand implementation is established. Each of the seven response dimensions remains unknown.

february_boundary.summary: Search-only titles in Feb report a 72nd through 78th day; they do not establish a subsequent end date or independent corroboration.

notes: This is a December-started continuity/boundary lead, not a new January-started event. The manual threshold, domestic state/policy target, event ownership and episode end remain unresolved. Repeated daily titles are not counted as separate events or independent sources. The late-February titles are search-only.

title: Karabakh-Armenian delegation at Russian peacekeeping checkpoint
location: Lachin Corridor checkpoint in Nagorno-Karabakh; TIME describes the territory as inside internationally recognized Azerbaijan borders but under de facto Artsakh administration.
organizer: A delegation of Karabakh Armenians, as described in TIME.
demands: Reopen the road; the delegation addressed Russian peacekeepers.
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance count; 50-person threshold not established.

date.summary: TIME dates this distinct delegation to Dec 24, 2022.

demand_and_target.summary: The delegation asked Russian peacekeepers to reopen the road.

attendance_threshold.summary: Described as a delegation, with no headcount.

location.summary: The article distinguishes recognized borders, de facto administration and Russian peacekeeping control.

notes: Outside January. This is a separate lead from the Azerbaijani sit-in and is not merged with the later march. The recipient is a foreign peacekeeping force; territory/ownership remains politically contested, so no automatic country transfer. The reported occurrence date does not establish when the gathering physically ended.

title: Karabakh-Armenian march to Russian peacekeeping headquarters
location: Russian peacekeeping headquarters in Nagorno-Karabakh; TIME places the territory within internationally recognized Azerbaijan borders but describes de facto Artsakh administration.
organizer: Karabakh-Armenian residents, as described in TIME.
demands: A demand for answers from Russian peacekeepers is reported; no demand against Azerbaijan’s government is established.
participants_original: dozens of men, women, and children
threshold_50_evidence: Source says dozens; it does not establish 50 or more.

date.summary: TIME says this was three days after its separately dated Dec 24 delegation; Dec 27 is derived from that sequence.

demand_and_target.summary: The account concerns answers from Russian peacekeepers.

attendance_threshold.summary: Reported as dozens, which does not establish the 50-person threshold.

location.summary: Location is described amid Azerbaijan’s recognized borders, de facto Artsakh governance and Russian peacekeeper control.

notes: Outside January and distinct from the Dec 24 delegation and Dec 12 Azerbaijani sit-in. Date is derived from TIME’s relative wording; no independent date source. Foreign target and territorial ownership remain unresolved; no automatic country transfer. The reported occurrence date does not establish when the gathering physically ended.
